title: ORPHAN, a game engine in C
description:
The engine SPASTAZ, UPLINK, AISLE 666 and my other recent games run on. It's built the way engines were made around 2002: a drop-down console with cvars and binds, game.exe +map dm1 command lines, maps made in a separate editor (Spade), and an SDK editor that ties a game together, Orphan Workshop.
A game is a C program that hands the engine a few functions, and the engine runs the rest. The Workshop has tabs for code (with build, play and errors on their lines), live-compiling shaders, placing your game's entities on a map, and tools for assets, maps, mods, profiler captures and crash reports. New Project starts from a full first-person starter game or one of the smaller examples: a shooting range, a hover-car racer and a 2D vector arcade game.
howItWorks:
Built on raylib, with box3d physics, Lua 5.4, enet networking, OpenAL Soft and discord-rpc.
Every game on it can host and join out of the box, over LAN or a direct address, and never talks to any server of ours. Steam (presence, achievements, join from your friends list) and Discord are optional.
It builds natively on Windows with MSYS2, or cross-compiles the same Windows exes from Linux and WSL with mingw-w64, recompiling only what changed.
